problem:
A shipping container of mass $5\,000\,\text{kg}$ is released from rest and falls vertically downward. Let $v(t)$ be the container's velocity, in meters per second, $t\ge 0$ seconds after release, with downward taken as the positive direction.
The air resistance on the container is proportional to the square of its velocity and acts in the direction opposite to its motion.
At a particular moment during the fall, the container’s velocity is $12.5\,\text{m/s}$ and its instantaneous acceleration is $7.35\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.$

Find, rounded to two decimal places, the velocity of the container after $3$ seconds.
Assume the acceleration due to gravity is $g=9.8\,{\text{m/s}}^{2},$ and the only forces acting on the container are the weight due to gravity and drag.

activity_context.topic_title: Falling Body Problems With Quadratic Drag
